_meta.purpose: Single source of truth for CushLabs commercial terms — price, trial, cancellation, billing, invoicing, and delivery timing.
_meta.why_this_exists: These claims kept drifting because they were retyped as prose on every surface that needed them. In one week: the homepage promised 'Cancel Anytime' and then '30 days notice' while the contract required neither; USD surfaces promised a CFDI, which is a Mexican tax receipt a US client does not receive; 'Live in days, not weeks' appeared in the footer, the hero and the meta description while the same homepage showed '2-6 wks'. Every time, a source document was already correct and a second surface had drifted from it. Reading a document is optional; importing data is not.
_meta.how_to_use: Do NOT retype these values into components. Import them. cushlabs runs `npm run sync:terms`, which copies this file to src/data/commercialTerms.json, and components read from there. `npm run validate:terms` fails the build when a surface contradicts this file.
consumers: cushlabs-messenger-bot — anything the assistant says about price or terms

currency_rule.statement: MXN and USD are separate price lists, not conversions of one another.
currency_rule.never: Never auto-convert MXN to USD or back. The USD list is its own decision.
currency_rule.mxn_tax_note: ALL MXN prices are quoted plus IVA. Locked 2026-08-13.

trial.why_wording_matters: The pricing page and ADVERTISED-COMMITMENTS both say '1 week'. Saying '7-day' elsewhere is the same duration in different words, and a prospect comparing two surfaces cannot tell whether they are two offers.
trial.starts: the day the assistant goes live, not the day the client signs
trial.walk_away: If it is not doing what was agreed, the client owes nothing.

cancellation.effective: end of the current paid month
cancellation.statement_en: Cancel whenever you want: it takes effect at the end of the month you have already paid for, and there is nothing else to settle.
cancellation.statement_es: Cancela cuando quieras: aplica al terminar el mes que ya pagaste, y no queda nada más por saldar.
cancellation.why: Billing is monthly IN ADVANCE, so the month in progress is already paid. Cancelling means no next invoice — there is no refund exposure and no unbilled work. A notice period would collect a further month after a client said stop.

billing.paypal_note: Added 2026-09-25, Robert's decision, to unblock the US market. Bank transfer means SPEI in Mexico, which is free and is how the one paying client settles today; asking a US small business to wire money to Mexico is where a $129/mo deal dies instead. PayPal is the US rail because it supports recurring billing natively and US buyers already trust it. WHAT IT COSTS DEPENDS ENTIRELY ON WHERE IT SETTLES, and that is the whole question: a US-registered PayPal paying out USD to a US bank account is a domestic transaction with no currency conversion at all, while a Mexico-registered one collecting the same dollars stacks a cross-border fee and an FX spread on top. Robert holds a US bank account, so the domestic path is available and is the one to use. Confirm which registration the PayPal account actually has before quoting any margin; the rate itself is not recorded here because it moves.
billing.zelle_note: Available and free, not yet formally adopted as a method. Robert holds a US bank account, so Zelle is US-bank-to-US-bank at zero cost — materially cheaper than PayPal for the first few clients. Its limits are real and decide when it stops being the answer: no recurring billing, so every month is manual; per-day caps set by the bank; and some US businesses' payables processes will not pay a vendor by Zelle at all and will want an invoice. Fine at one to three clients, wrong at ten.
billing.card_note: Card processing is NOT live in any currency. Confirmed 2026-08-06, still true 2026-09-25. Any surface saying 'pay by card' is wrong. The Stripe Mexico ACCOUNT is verified (capability-registry: stripe-mx-account-verification) and that is not the same thing as checkout being live — do not read the approval as a working rail.
billing.us_cost_warning: COLLECT US DOLLARS INTO THE US ACCOUNT, NOT THROUGH MEXICO. A US card charged through Stripe Mexico stacks international and conversion surcharges on the domestic rate — tier-feature-spec.md 4.2 records international cards adding 0.5% and required currency conversion a further 2% over a 4.35-4.45% base, so roughly 7% all-in on a USD subscription. Routing the same dollars into the US account instead avoids the conversion entirely: Zelle is free, and a US-registered PayPal is charged at domestic rates. The choice of receiving account, not the choice of processor, is what decides the cost. The tax and reporting consequences of US-sourced business income for a Mexican tax resident are an accountant's question and are deliberately not answered here.

mexico.note: IVA itemized on the CFDI. This is what makes the payment deductible in Mexico.

outside_mexico.note: NOT a CFDI. A CFDI is a Mexican SAT tax receipt and is meaningless to a US buyer. Confirmed by Robert 2026-08-20.
outside_mexico.taxes: determined in the individual service agreement

complex.statement_en: More complex integrations typically take 2 to 6 weeks.

delivery_timing.combined_en: Simple setups launch in days; more complex integrations typically take 2 to 6 weeks.
delivery_timing.combined_es: Las configuraciones simples se lanzan en días; las integraciones más complejas suelen tomar de 2 a 6 semanas.
never_say: en vivo en días, no semanas
delivery_timing.why: 'Days, not weeks' was in the footer of every page, the hero, /about/ and the homepage meta description — while the same homepage showed '2-6 wks - Time to Live'. It promised a timeline some projects cannot hit.
